newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Gunmen run amok in Albanian hospital.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen run amok in Albanian hospital.

text.p: Dozens of gunmen ran amok at a hospital in this southern Albanian town as they grieved over the death of a friend, shot by accident like dozens of others in this violence-plagued country.

As many as 40 gunmen burst into the operating room of the hospital on Wednesday night and fired wildly after the victim was brought in, riddling the walls with bullet holes and smashing windows, doctors said.
"There is no safety here," hospital director Agim Bezati told Reuters. No one was hurt in the 30-minute outburst at the hospital in Lushnje, 85 km (50 miles) south of Tirana.

Metan Sula, a 35-year-old businessman, died when a friend gestured to him with a pistol to join him in a ride, playfully pressed the trigger in the belief that it was unloaded, and shot him through the heart.
He was the latest of nearly 300 people who have died in the violence that swept this impoverished Balkan country sparked by popular anger over failed pyramid savings schemes.

The majority of the victims were killed, like the latest one, in accidental shootings by civilians mishandling weapons looted from army barracks after the army melted away in the face of an anti-government uprising in the south that spread through the whole country.
The man who pulled the trigger fled and is now in hiding, doctors said.
"Everyone has guns here," said Bezati. "Medical staff are not protected."
About 30 patients and the two armed guards at the drab, two-storey hospital fled during the rampage. Bezati said several returned on Thursday morning and he expected most back by the end of the day.
Some of the patients who fled had infectious diseases and others had heart problems, diabetes and ulcers.
In the near-anarachy that currently reigns in Albania, hospitals have often been targeted by the gunmen.
In the northern town of Shkoder, two doctors were shot inside the main hospital recently, one of whom died several days later.
Another man was shot to death on an operating table in the middle of an emergency operation for a gunshot wound.
A truck of the Geneva-based International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) arrived at Lushnje hospital on Thursday morning to deliver food and emergency medical supplies.
"We are hoping to do everything we can to help these people who are in desperate need of food and medicine," said Barbara Jaggi, a Red Cross officer.
She said the ICRC, who distribute aid without armed escorts, had brought food, antibiotics, bandages and surgical supplies to Lushnje hospital.
"We are only bringing a small amount of supplies because we don't want the hospital to run the risk of being looted," she added.
